**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

n**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

,**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

 **Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

 **Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

a**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

e**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds

them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

q**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

:**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

y**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

t**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

h**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

g**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

 **Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

 **Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds

them off and on.

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

r**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

e**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

 **Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

e**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

n**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

e**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

o**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

e**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

r**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

c**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

them off and on.

`**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

 **Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

e**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

e**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

.**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

a**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

a**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds

flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

i**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

/**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

h**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

e**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

m**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch

lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

c**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

 **Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

h**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

f**Lights.** Each car has a headlight, ditch lights L and R and markers, as
light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.

light functions (A headlight, A ditch L, ...) that relays and board pins map
to. They follow 49 CFR 229.125. At the leading car the headlight and ditch
lights burn steady. The ditch lights flash alternately (L / R) when the horn
sounds at grade crossings (229.125(d)): here they flash while the horn sounds
or the Crossing sequence runs, and for 15 s after the last horn (the rule lets
them continue until the train is past). The trailing car shows its markers,
with its headlight and ditch lights off. Settings → Light functions sets the
flash rate (40-180 per minute per lamp, default 60) and how long the flashing
lasts after the horn. The engineer page's ☀ Lights button switches all of
them off and on.
